overview.musicalIdentity: Lagos’s pilot history distinguishes Fela Kuti’s Afrobeat from the later Afrobeats umbrella and includes the city’s Shrine tradition, political performance history, and Alté-era experimentation.

listenHereStatus.reason: Pilot recordings and sound guides are metadata/description-only until playback rights are independently resolved.

data.name: Alté
data.summary: A Nigerian alternative scene/genre label coined by DRB LasGidi in 2014 and associated with cross-genre experimentation in Lagos and beyond.

data.name: Afrobeat
data.summary: A genre pioneered by Fela Kuti that combined African musical traditions with funk, jazz, rock and related diasporic influences, and became deeply linked with Lagos cultural and political life.

data.name: Afrobeat as political performance
data.summary: Fela’s Lagos-based Afrobeat combined music and anti-establishment political expression, making the scene inseparable from postcolonial social history.

data.name: Afrobeats
data.summary: A broad, fluid umbrella for contemporary West African pop sounds, distinct from Fela Kuti’s singular Afrobeat genre.

data.name: Tenor saxophone in Fela’s Afrobeat practice
data.summary: The Kalakuta Museum preserves Fela Kuti’s painted signature tenor saxophone, making the instrument a tangible link to his performance practice.

data.summary: Afrobeat’s ensemble sound prominently uses layered percussion alongside horns, rhythm section and call-and-response vocals.

Africa Shrine opens at the Empire Hotel site

metadata.relationship_note: Fela’s archive documents the Shrine as a core performance/political space during Afrobeat’s development.
The museum occupies Fela’s former Kalakuta home and preserves objects from his life and career.
Fela’s family built the New Afrika Shrine to preserve Fela and the original Shrine’s community/cultural legacy.
